numerical_failure.observed_behavior: get_period_ordinal is declared noexcept, so the OverflowError raised by np_datetime.c for an ordinal that does not fit in int64 was discarded (Cython printed 'Exception ignored in: pandas._libs.tslibs.period.get_period_ordinal' to stderr) and ordinal 0 was returned, e.g. Period('2300-01-01', freq='ns') gave Period('1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000000', 'ns'); PeriodIndex(['2000-01-01','2300-01-01','2001-01-01'], freq='ns').asi8 gave array([946684800000000000, 0, 978307200000000000]); date_range('2300-01-01', periods=2, freq='D', unit='s').to_period('ns') gave 1970 epoch periods.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Out-of-range ordinals should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime instead of silently returning the 1970 epoch; all three examples now raise OutOfBoundsDatetime.
trigger_conditions: ordinal for the datetime does not fit in int64 (e.g. year 2300 with freq='ns')
fine-grained freq such as ns used for Period construction
int and object array paths to PeriodIndex
oracle_clues: Cython 'Exception ignored in' message on stderr
all three cases now raise OutOfBoundsDatetime

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Period("2300-01-01", freq="ns") and the int/object array path with year 2300 overflow int64 nanosecond ordinal; the overflow OverflowError was discarded and ordinal 0 (1970 epoch) returned
category_specific_evidence: get_period_ordinal is noexcept, so the OverflowError raised by np_datetime.c for an ordinal that does not fit in int64 was discarded and ordinal 0 returned in its place
Period("2300-01-01", freq="ns"), the int and object array paths, and DatetimeIndex.to_period("ns") all gave a 1970 epoch period

Test test_constructor_int_array_out_of_bounds_ordinal uses arr = np.array([2000, 2300, 2001]) with dtype int64 and object, expects OutOfBoundsDatetime with message "Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 2300-01-01" for PeriodIndex(arr, freq="ns")
Previously the overflow gave a 1970 epoch entry in the middle of valid ones (GH#64158)
Fix validates before converting; freq-dependent bounds are hoisted out of loops with one year comparison per element, boundary years use check_dts_bounds
SAFE_MIN_YEAR/SAFE_MAX_YEAR are lower.year+1 and upper.year-1 per unit, so boundary years still get the exact check
Performance: PR timings on 1M values show small changes (e.g. to_period("ns") 18.2 ms main vs 18.3 ms PR; to_period("M") 12.1 ms vs 13.0 ms)
period_ordinal lacked initialization of dts.as, fixed with memset because bounds check reads it
reproduction_risks: The PR body is truncated mid-sentence about GH-66550 test for to_period("ns") on wall time at NaT sentinel, so that expectation is unknown
Passing integer data emits a Pandas4Warning, filtered in the test; warning behavior must be accounted for
Boundary years for ns are not fully given in the passages beyond the 2300 example
